meta.title: Present Perfect Tenses
meta.description: A comprehensive test covering English Present Perfect Tenses for GenZ.
meta.info: This test includes 30 questions focusing on combined grammar structures involving the Present Perfect tense paired with topics like relative clauses, gerunds, passive voice, conditionals, quantifiers, and more, all within familiar Gen Z contexts.
meta.author: Qwen3.7

data.hint: Choose the correct verb forms to complete the sentence.
data.question: The K-pop group, which _____ three albums this year, _____ incredibly popular among Gen Z.

explanation.text: This combines the Present Perfect tense with non-defining relative clauses. The singular subject 'group' requires the singular Present Perfect 'has released' and 'has become'.
explanation.concept: Subject-verb agreement in relative clauses using Present Perfect
explanation.formula: Singular noun, which + has + past participle, + has + past participle
examples: The band, which has released two singles, has become famous.

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

explanation.text: This combines the Present Perfect tense with quantifiers and subject-verb agreement. 'Several of the brands' is plural, requiring 'have launched'. 'Much of the inventory' is uncountable and singular, requiring 'has sold'.
explanation.concept: Agreement with plural and uncountable quantifiers in Present Perfect
explanation.formula: Plural quantifier + plural noun + have + past participle; Uncountable quantifier + singular noun + has + past participle
examples: Many of the items have sold out, but much of the stock has remained.

data.hint: Choose the correct verb forms to complete the sentence.
data.question: Since he started streaming, he _____ _____ toxic games to keep his community positive.

explanation.text: This combines the Present Perfect tense with gerund verb patterns. The singular subject 'he' requires 'has avoided', and the verb 'avoid' is always followed by a gerund ('playing').
explanation.concept: Present Perfect actions and verbs followed by gerunds
explanation.formula: Subject + has/have + past participle + verb-ing
examples: She has avoided eating sugar since last year.

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

explanation.text: This combines the Present Perfect tense with the passive voice. The subject 'several features' receives the action, so it requires the Present Perfect passive 'have been removed', not the active 'have removed'.
explanation.concept: Present Perfect passive constructions
explanation.formula: Plural subject + have been + past participle
examples: The posts have been deleted by the moderators.

data.hint: Choose the correct prepositions to complete the sentence.
data.question: Many teenagers have become more aware _____ their mental health, and they have started talking _____ it openly.

explanation.text: This combines the Present Perfect tense with adjective and verb preposition collocations. 'Aware' is followed by 'of', and 'talking' (in this context) is followed by 'about'.
explanation.concept: Correct preposition usage after specific adjectives and verbs
explanation.formula: Have/has become aware of + noun; have/has started talking about + noun
examples: They have become aware of the issue and are talking about it.

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

explanation.text: This combines the Present Perfect in a time/condition clause with a Third Conditional main clause. The hypothetical past result requires 'would have joined', while 'haven't had' correctly uses the Present Perfect to describe a past-to-present lack of time.
explanation.concept: Mixing Present Perfect facts with hypothetical past conditionals
explanation.formula: If + subject + present perfect, subject + would have + past participle
examples: If I have finished my work, I would have gone out (Note: Standard mixed conditional logic applies here for hypothetical past results).

data.hint: Choose the correct conjunction to complete the sentence.
data.question: _____ the anime has received mixed reviews, it has still managed to build a massive fanbase online.

explanation.text: This combines the Present Perfect tense with concessive conjunctions. 'Although' introduces a contrast between the mixed reviews and the massive fanbase, both described using the Present Perfect.
explanation.concept: Using concessive conjunctions with Present Perfect clauses
explanation.formula: Although + subject + has/have + past participle, subject + has/have + past participle
examples: Although it has rained, we have enjoyed the trip.

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

explanation.text: This combines the Present Perfect tense with advanced comparatives. 'Better' is already the comparative form of 'good', so 'more' is redundant and must be removed.
explanation.concept: Correct comparative forms in Present Perfect sentences
explanation.formula: Subject + has/have + past participle + better + noun
examples: She has drawn better sketches this month.

data.hint: Choose the correct modal and verb forms to complete the sentence.
data.question: You _____ seen the new crypto regulations; they _____ been implemented just last week.

explanation.text: This combines the Present Perfect with modal verbs of deduction. 'Must have' expresses a strong logical deduction about the past, and 'they' (plural) requires 'have' in the Present Perfect passive.
explanation.concept: Modal perfect for deduction and Present Perfect passive agreement
explanation.formula: Subject + must have + past participle; plural subject + have + been + past participle
examples: You must have seen the news; it has been reported everywhere.

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

explanation.text: This combines the Present Perfect tense with time clauses. 'Since' triggers the Present Perfect. The word order for the adverb 'never' in the Present Perfect is between the auxiliary 'have' and the past participle 'regretted'.
explanation.concept: Adverb placement in Present Perfect sentences
explanation.formula: Since + present perfect, subject + have + never + past participle
examples: Since I have started this job, I have never regretted it.

data.hint: Choose the correct verb forms to complete the sentence.
data.question: I have considered _____ a monstera plant, but I have avoided _____ one because I don't have enough sunlight.

explanation.text: This combines the Present Perfect tense with gerund verb patterns. Both 'consider' and 'avoid' are verbs that must be followed by a gerund ('buying', 'getting').
explanation.concept: Specific verbs requiring gerund complements
explanation.formula: Have/has considered + verb-ing; have/has avoided + verb-ing
examples: I have considered moving, but I have avoided deciding yet.

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

explanation.text: This combines the Present Perfect passive with quantifiers and subject-verb agreement. 'Coffee beans' is a countable plural noun, requiring 'Many of' and the plural auxiliary 'have'.
explanation.concept: Countable vs. uncountable quantifiers with Present Perfect
explanation.formula: Many of + plural countable noun + have + been + past participle
examples: Many of the books have been read.

data.hint: Choose the correct verb forms to complete the sentence.
data.question: The new Pilates studio _____ by many influencers, and several classes _____ fully booked already.

explanation.text: This combines the Present Perfect passive with subject-verb agreement. 'Studio' is singular, requiring 'has been visited'. 'Classes' is plural, requiring 'have been'.
explanation.topic: Present Perfect + Passive Voice + Subject-Verb Agreement
explanation.concept: Singular and plural agreement in Present Perfect passive
explanation.formula: Singular subject + has been + past participle; plural subject + have been + past participle
examples: The room has been cleaned, and the chairs have been arranged.

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

explanation.text: This combines the Present Perfect tense with preposition collocations and infinitive patterns. 'Obsessed' is followed by 'with', and 'relied on it' is followed by the to-infinitive 'to protect' to express purpose.
explanation.concept: Correct preposition and infinitive usage after specific verbs/adjectives
explanation.formula: Have been obsessed with + noun; have relied on + noun + to-infinitive
examples: I have been obsessed with this game, and I have relied on it to relax.

data.hint: Choose the correct verb forms to complete the sentence.
data.question: The author, whose latest novel _____ the BookTok charts for weeks, _____ a massive following among young readers.

explanation.text: This combines the Present Perfect tense with possessive relative clauses. The singular subject 'novel' requires 'has topped', and the singular subject 'author' requires 'has gained'.
explanation.concept: Subject-verb agreement in possessive relative clauses
explanation.formula: Singular noun, whose + singular noun + has + past participle, + has + past participle
examples: The singer, whose song has topped the charts, has gained fame.

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

explanation.text: This combines a Third Conditional hypothetical past with a Present Perfect factual statement. The hypothetical past condition requires the Past Perfect 'If I had learned', while the contrasting fact uses the Present Perfect 'I have only started'.
explanation.concept: Contrasting hypothetical past conditions with present perfect facts
explanation.formula: If + subject + had + past participle, subject + would have + past participle, but + subject + has/have + past participle
examples: If I had known, I would have helped, but I have only found out now.

data.hint: Choose the correct verb forms to complete the sentence.
data.question: This year's festival lineup is _____ exciting than last year's, and more artists _____ confirmed to perform.

explanation.text: This combines comparatives with the Present Perfect passive. 'Far more' is the correct intensifier for the comparative 'exciting', and the plural subject 'artists' requires 'have been confirmed'.
explanation.concept: Intensifying comparatives and plural agreement in Present Perfect passive
explanation.formula: Far more + adjective + than; plural subject + have been + past participle
examples: This movie is far more interesting, and many scenes have been praised.

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

explanation.text: This combines the Present Perfect tense with gerund verb patterns. 'Finish' and the expression 'can't stop' must both be followed by a gerund ('listening', 'thinking').
explanation.concept: Verbs and expressions requiring gerund complements
explanation.formula: Have finished + verb-ing; can't stop + verb-ing
examples: I have finished reading, and I can't stop thinking about it.

data.hint: Choose the correct quantifiers to complete the sentence.
data.question: _____ of the thrifted items have been upcycled creatively, and _____ of the waste has been reduced significantly.

explanation.text: This combines the Present Perfect passive with quantifiers. 'Items' is a countable plural noun, requiring 'Many'. 'Waste' is an uncountable noun, requiring 'much'.
explanation.concept: Countable vs. uncountable quantifiers with Present Perfect
explanation.formula: Many of + plural countable noun + have been; much of + uncountable noun + has been
examples: Many of the books have been sold, and much of the time has been saved.

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

explanation.text: This combines modal perfect deduction with the Present Perfect passive and relative clauses. 'Must have' must be followed by the past participle 'seen', not the past simple 'saw'.
explanation.topic: Present Perfect + Modal Verbs + Relative Clauses
explanation.concept: Past participle form after modal perfects
explanation.formula: Subject + must have + past participle
examples: You must have heard the news that has been shared.

data.hint: Choose the correct verb forms to complete the sentence.
data.question: Since I _____ Duolingo, I _____ my vocabulary significantly, and I have maintained a 100-day streak.

explanation.text: This combines the Present Perfect tense in both the 'since' clause and the main clause to show an action that started in the past and continues to have relevance in the present.
explanation.concept: Using Present Perfect in 'since' clauses for ongoing relevance
explanation.formula: Since + subject + has/have + past participle, subject + has/have + past participle
examples: Since I have moved here, I have made many friends.

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

explanation.text: This combines the Present Perfect tense with concessive conjunctions. 'Although' is required to show the contrast between trying veganism and missing cheese, rather than 'Because', which would imply causation.
explanation.concept: Using concessive conjunctions to show contrast with Present Perfect
explanation.formula: Although + subject + has/have + past participle, subject + has/have + past participle
examples: Although I have tried it, I have missed it.

data.hint: Choose the correct verb forms to complete the sentence.
data.question: Several universities _____ new scholarships for international students, and many applications _____ already processed.

explanation.text: This combines the Present Perfect active and passive voices with subject-verb agreement. 'Universities' is plural, requiring 'have introduced'. 'Applications' is plural, requiring 'have been processed'.
explanation.topic: Present Perfect + Passive Voice + Subject-Verb Agreement
explanation.concept: Plural agreement in Present Perfect active and passive
explanation.formula: Plural subject + have + past participle; plural subject + have been + past participle
examples: The managers have approved the plans, and the documents have been signed.

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

explanation.text: This combines the Present Perfect tense with preposition collocations. The adjective 'interested' is always followed by the preposition 'in', not 'on'.
explanation.concept: Correct preposition usage after specific adjectives
explanation.formula: Have/has been interested in + noun
examples: I have been interested in art for years.

data.hint: Choose the correct verb forms to complete the sentence.
data.question: The esports team, which _____ the regional championship twice, _____ a reputation for their incredible teamwork.

explanation.text: This combines the Present Perfect tense with non-defining relative clauses. The collective noun 'team' is treated as singular here, requiring 'has won' and 'has built'.
explanation.concept: Singular agreement for collective nouns in relative clauses
explanation.formula: Singular collective noun, which + has + past participle, + has + past participle
examples: The committee, which has met twice, has decided the outcome.

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

explanation.text: This combines the Present Perfect tense with gerund verb patterns. The verb 'avoid' must be followed by a gerund ('checking'), not a to-infinitive.
explanation.concept: Verbs requiring gerund complements in Present Perfect
explanation.formula: Have/has avoided + verb-ing
examples: I have avoided eating sugar.

data.hint: Choose the correct verb forms to complete the sentence.
data.question: This indie game has received _____ positive reviews than the AAA titles, and its player base _____ grown exponentially.

explanation.text: This combines the Present Perfect tense with advanced comparatives. 'Far more' is the correct intensifier for the comparative 'positive reviews', and the singular subject 'player base' requires 'has grown'.
explanation.concept: Intensifying comparatives and singular agreement in Present Perfect
explanation.formula: Has received + far more + plural noun + than; singular subject + has + past participle
examples: It has received far more attention, and its popularity has surged.

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

explanation.text: This combines the Present Perfect tense with quantifiers and subject-verb agreement. 'Workers' is a countable plural noun, requiring 'Few of'. 'Companies' is plural, requiring 'have implemented'.
explanation.concept: Countable quantifiers and plural agreement in Present Perfect
explanation.formula: Few of + plural countable noun + have + past participle; many of + plural noun + have + past participle
examples: Few of the students have passed, and many of the teachers have agreed.

data.hint: Choose the correct modal and verb forms to complete the sentence.
data.question: She _____ read your tarot cards by now; she _____ been practicing for years.

explanation.text: This combines the Present Perfect with modal verbs of deduction. 'Must have' expresses a strong logical deduction about a completed action, and the singular subject 'she' requires 'has' in the Present Perfect continuous.
explanation.concept: Modal perfect for deduction and Present Perfect continuous agreement
explanation.formula: Subject + must have + past participle; singular subject + has + been + verb-ing
examples: He must have finished; he has been working all day.

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

explanation.text: This combines a Third Conditional hypothetical past with a Present Perfect factual statement. The hypothetical past condition requires the Past Perfect 'If I had known', while the contrasting fact uses the Present Perfect 'have only discovered'.
explanation.concept: Contrasting hypothetical past conditions with present perfect facts
explanation.formula: If + subject + had + past participle, subject + would have + past participle, but + subject + has/have + past participle
examples: If I had known, I would have helped, but I have only found out now.
